issue_context.title: Physically locking/unlocking lock indicates inverse transition states
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Level Locks (Bolt) paired via HomeKit Controller show inverse behavior with associated lock entity when physically operated.  When the deadbolt is physically unlocked, the lock entity transitions to "locking" and will stay that way indefinitely.  Physically locking the lock will change the state back to "locked".  If the lock is in an unlocked state, physically locking it will transition the lock entity to "unlocking" where it will stay that way indefinitely.  Physically unlocking the lock will change the state back to "unlocked."  The transition states can be cleared by clicking "lock/unlock" in the UI.  This inverse transition state behavior only manifests itself when physically interacting with the lock.  Control via HA UI always reports the correct transition and end states.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.11.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

HomeKit Controller

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/homekit_controller/

### Diagnostics information

[homekit_controller-82eb43465048e061726399c7778b3236-A94923PF-87ee40677e797fd73acbe8f7cf195a42.json.txt](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/9975059/homekit_controller-82eb43465048e061726399c7778b3236-A94923PF-87ee40677e797fd73acbe8f7cf195a42.json.txt)


### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

Per HomeKit Controller release notes for 2022.11.0, these locks were unpaired and re-paired as duplicate entities did appear post upgrade.  Additionally, unpaired and re-paired under 2022.11.2 and issue persists.

Its a different issue and its a frontend problem: https://github.com/home-assistant/frontend/pull/14359
Whats going on here is the lock is only broadcasting the current state and the target state is never changing so it stays stuck in an operation.

It looks like a bug in the lock firmware

So if you locked it via HA, the target state becomes secured, and then you physically unlock it the target state remains secured but the current state is now notified as unsecured so the lock is in a locking state
.. and since the lock never sends a new target state you end up with locking or unlocking when you physically change the state

Yes, just tested and that's a correct assumption.

~~I suppose, with that knowledge a basic automation could be written to do just that, as a short-term fix.~~
